text:
hana: heads-up — onboarding sample app (Flask dev server on Windows) crashes when it tries to use AsyncClient during app startup. Error is weird: `RuntimeError: Event loop policy cannot be changed` followed by `RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop` in different repros.

omar: can you paste the minimal snippet?

hana: minimal repro is in the sample-app startup hook:
```py
# app.py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()
# synchronous startup hook that calls a convenience helper
resp = client.chat.completions.create(model="rwd-1", input="hi")
print(resp.output_text)
```
If I run `python app.py` on Windows I sometimes see an exception coming from `asyncio.set_event_loop_policy()` deep in httpx/uvloop detection. On other runs it's `asyncio.run()` complaining because Flask's reloader spawns threads and interacts with the loop.

ben: hmm this is several layers: (1) we're mixing sync module-level calls that call into our convenience wrappers (which use asyncio.run under the hood), (2) on Windows event loop policy defaults are different (Proactor) and some libs try to set a policy which raises if already set, (3) dev servers/reloaders spawn processes/threads which makes lifecycle fragile.

omar: agree. We should never start network/async work at import time in sample apps. The sample-app quickstart should show creating the client inside an `if __name__ == \"__main__\"` or in a proper lifecycle hook (Flask's `before_first_request`, or FastAPI startup event).

hana: also noticed that our sync convenience helpers attempt to set an event loop policy for performance (we had a conditional `if platform != 'win32': uvloop.install()` style). That conditional sometimes still calls `set_event_loop_policy` indirectly via httpx/anyio on Windows in nested runtimes. If the policy is changed after a loop exists, you get `RuntimeError`.

ben: proposed immediate actions: 1) docs change: add a \"Do not call client at import time\" note and show safe patterns for Flask, FastAPI, and CLI scripts; 2) SDK change: make sync wrappers avoid touching loop policies and avoid calling `asyncio.run` at import-level; instead raise a clear error if used in a running event loop and suggest `async with AsyncClient()` or `await` usage; 3) add a lint rule to sample apps that warns about top-level network calls.

omar: also add a small CI scenario on Windows runner that starts the sample-app in dev mode to catch reloader-related failures. I can draft a tiny GH Actions job.

hana: filed issue #2101: \"Sample app import-time AsyncClient calls cause event-loop policy and asyncio.run errors on Windows/dev servers\" with repro and small sample app.

ben: one more DX tweak: improve error text when our convenience helper detects a running loop. Instead of the generic `asyncio.run` error, raise ``RuntimeError(\"AsyncClient sync helper called inside running event loop. Use `await` or `async with AsyncClient()`; see docs: <link>\")``. That would save a lot of troubleshoot time.

omar: yes please. Also add a typing note: some editors hide that `create()` returns a coroutine because we have mixed sync/async classes. We should fix the stubs so the async client's methods are properly annotated as Awaitable -> editors will show `await` in completions.

devx-bot: task created: T-512 \"Prevent import-time AsyncClient usage in sample-apps + Windows CI job\".

docs-bot: created issue #2101 with repro and linked docs PR template.

hana: thanks — I'll validate the Windows CI once the job is up. For the short term I've updated the sample-app readme to move the example into a startup function and added a note about not mutating event loop policy on Windows. :thumbsup:
